title: Tamsin and the Veil
premise: Edmund Galloway has spent a decade hiding their beast-speaker gift behind guild ledgers, invisible in the border city of Vaelmoor. When the wards collapse and the stars go dark, Edmund learns the king is bound to an ancient entity called the Veil, which feeds on names and erases those who hear it spoken. Forced to ally with a disgraced warden and a starless constellation given human form, Edmund must choose between exposing their gift—and themselves—to save the realm, or staying silent while everyone they love is unmade. In the end, Edmund gives up their own name to the Veil to free the king, surviving as someone new: remembered by beasts, half-remembered by friends, and finally at peace with being no one and something entirely their own.
about_author: Tamsin Nystrom grew up on a failing sheep farm above the fog line, where she claims she learned to talk to animals out of boredom rather than magic. She writes fantasy about quiet people forced into loud destinies, and still keeps bees that do not, as far as anyone can prove, answer back.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A night of routine bookkeeping in the Gilded Scale guild, cataloging impossible trades—a bottled echo, a moth that remembers futures—while concealing the fact that Edmund can hear the guild's caged beasts begging. Establishes Edmund's careful invisibility and loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of a self kept under lock.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Bones
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The border wards hum wrong; beasts within ten miles fall silent at once, a silence only Edmund notices. Guildmaster Corvane dismisses concerns, and Edmund overhears him trading something with a hooded buyer whose voice sounds like many voices. Emotional beat: dread creeping through ordinary walls.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Every star goes out simultaneously; the wards shatter like glass. In the panic, a stablehorse speaks Edmund's true name aloud—something no one living knows—proving the Veil is already reading the city. Emotional beat: terror and the first crack in Edmund's hiding.

chapters.title: A Warden With Nothing Left
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. Introduce Sera, a disgraced border warden blamed for the wards' failure, drunk in a gutter shrine when Edmund finds her tracking the silence. They strike a wary bargain: her knowledge of ward-craft, Edmund's access to the guild's forbidden inventory. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Know
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund risks the gift openly for the first time, questioning rats, ravens, and a dying elk. All describe 'the thing that eats names' walking north toward the capital wearing a king's shadow. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear—the gift makes Edmund visible at last.

chapters.title: The Guild's Price
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Corvane reveals he has been selling names to the Veil's agents for years to keep the guild prosperous, and orders Edmund to forget everything or be sold next. Edmund steals the ledger of sold names and flees with Sera. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: Road of Unremembered Villages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Traveling north, they find villages where residents have lost their own names and wander smiling, hollow. Sera teaches Edmund ward-theory; Edmund admits the truth of the gift. Emotional beat: intimacy built from shared damage.

chapters.title: The Star That Fell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They find a young woman, Lyra, standing in a crater—she was a constellation until the stars went out, now flesh and furious and losing memories by the hour. She joins them because the Veil devoured her sisters first. Emotional beat: grief wearing a defiant face.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Lyra's POV. Reaching the capital, they witness King Aldric at a public rite: adored, radiant, and utterly vacant, the Veil speaking through his mouth in a chorus. Lyra recognizes the entity as the devourer of constellations. Emotional beat: horror dressed in ceremony.

chapters.title: Ink and Old Promises
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the royal archive, Edmund deciphers that the first king bound the Veil with a sacrifice of names, renewed each generation—and this generation's renewal failed because Corvane sold the designated sacrifice's name years ago. Emotional beat: the past's debts coming due.

chapters.title: Hunted by Your Own Voice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Veil's agents, faceless clerks, hunt them using Edmund's stolen ledger. Sera is captured buying time; Edmund must choose rescue over the mission. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against survival, the book's central question made flesh.

chapters.title: The Bargaining Floor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund infiltrates the Veil's underground market to buy Sera back, offering the ledger of names. The Veil's broker counters: bring the king's binding-name, and both go free. Edmund lies and agrees. Emotional beat: becoming the kind of trader they always despised.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Menagerie
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Hiding in the royal menagerie, Edmund speaks with the king's old hunting hound, who remembers Aldric before the binding—and the moment the boy-king willingly let the Veil in to stop a plague. Emotional beat: compassion complicating the enemy.

chapters.title: Sera, Unbound
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Rescued but shaken, Sera confesses she didn't fail the wards—Corvane sabotaged them to force a crisis the Veil could exploit. Her shame transforms into purpose. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Chorus Speaks
chapters.summary: Lyra's POV. The Veil, sensing the plot, offers each of them their heart's desire in exchange for walking away: Sera's honor restored, Lyra's stars relit, Edmund's gift erased so they can be normal. Each refuses—but barely. Emotional beat: temptation as the sharpest blade.

chapters.title: Corvane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Confrontation with Corvane atop the guildhall; he believes serving the Veil is the only way Vaelmoor survives. Edmund uses the beasts' testimony—hundreds of voices—to strip his power and expose him publicly. Emotional beat: justice without satisfaction.

chapters.title: The Binding-Name
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They learn the binding-name required by the broker is the king's birth-name, held only in the memory of the dead first queen—reachable through the bottled echo Edmund once cataloged. A desperate retrieval through the guild's vaults. Emotional beat: hope assembled from scraps.

chapters.title: Throne of Many Mouths
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Climax begins: they breach the throne room during the Veil's coronation-renewal rite. The broker betrays them anyway; Sera holds the door against agents; Lyra burns what remains of her stellar light to blind the chorus. Emotional beat: sacrifice stacking on sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Given
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Climax. To unbind Aldric, a name of equal weight must be fed to the Veil. Edmund offers their own true name—the one the horse spoke in chapter three—freely, not as payment but as a gift, which the Veil cannot digest. The binding shatters; the king wakes screaming and human. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The stars return one by one; Lyra ascends rekindled but diminished, choosing mortality to stay with her friends. Sera is reinstated and refuses, founding instead an order of wardens who listen to beasts. Emotional beat: bittersweet dawn.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Call Me
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Nameless, Edmund discovers the beasts remember them perfectly, and people recall them as a warm impression rather than a person. Aldric, freed, seeks them out to say thank you to someone he cannot quite see. Emotional beat: grief and strange freedom entwined.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Veil
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Opening a new ledger in a rebuilt guild, Edmund chooses a new name for themselves—Tamsin—and writes the whole story down so it can never be eaten. The last line is spoken by every beast in Vaelmoor at once: welcome home. Emotional beat: identity remade, chosen at last.
